idea_text: Supermarkets and airports want their trolleys to stop working once someone pushes them off the premises, but a wheel that jams instantly can throw a person forward or get wrecked if they shove hard. My idea is a swivel wheel unit with a built-in lock that is triggered from outside: a small receiver in the wheel unit picks up a signal at the boundary, and a controller then engages the lock. The lock doesn't clamp the wheel dead, though. It works through a rotary damper, a housing with a little damping rotor inside that is linked to the wheel. When the lock engages, a stop feature on the housing catches the locking part, so the wheel can still turn but only against heavy resistance. You can still push the trolley along at a crawl for a short distance before it comes to a gentle halt, so nobody gets hurt and hard shoving can't break the wheel.

features.text: A swivel wheel unit for shopping, luggage or similar trolleys.
A receiver in the wheel unit picks up a boundary signal and a controller operates a lock.
A rotary damper: a housing with a damping rotor inside that is coupled to the wheel.
When locked, a stop on the damper housing holds the locking part, so the wheel turns only against resistance instead of stopping dead.
The gentle stop protects the user and stops hard shoving from breaking the wheel.
